title: Script It: Summarize an Access Log
description: Finish a half-written Bash script that turns an nginx access log into a report. ShellCheck clean, edge cases covered, fast on big logs. CI grades it.
summary: Finish a half-written Bash script that turns an nginx access log into a short report: requests, status classes, top clients and top paths. ShellCheck has to be clean and the edge cases right.
situation: When the site is slow, the first question on the incident call is always the same: who is hitting us, which pages, and how many errors?
Someone started summarize.sh to answer it from an nginx access log, then got pulled onto something else. Right now it counts lines and not much more, and ShellCheck is not happy with it.
task: Print the report described in the challenge README for a log in the combined format: requests, unique IPs, counts per status class, skipped lines, and the top IPs and paths.
Read the log from a file, or from stdin when no file is given or the file is -.
Support -n N for the length of the top lists, and exit 2 on usage errors and 1 on unreadable files, with messages on stderr.
Keep ShellCheck clean, without disable comments.

checks.name: ShellCheck is clean
checks.description: ShellCheck 0.11 reports no issues at any severity, and the script does not switch checks off with disable directives.

checks.name: Report for a known log
checks.description: Prints the exact report for a small log with a known answer.

checks.name: Edge cases
checks.description: Skips malformed lines, ignores empty lines, strips query strings, breaks ties in byte order, counts a last line with no newline and handles an empty log.

checks.name: File or stdin
checks.description: Reads the log from a file, from stdin when no file is given or the file is -, and from a file name with a space in it.

checks.name: Options and usage errors
checks.description: Supports -n N for the length of the top lists, and exits 2 with a message on stderr for a bad -n value, an unknown option or more than one file.

checks.name: Unreadable input
checks.description: Exits 1 with a message on stderr, and prints nothing on stdout, when the log file is missing, unreadable or a directory.

checks.name: Random logs
checks.description: Gives the right report for three logs generated at random during grading. Their names and answers are not visible to the script.

checks.name: Speed
checks.description: Summarizes a random 100,000-line log correctly in under 10 seconds, including about a second to start the container.

hints.title: Getting the edge cases right
hints.body: Match each line against the whole pattern before you use any of its fields, so a malformed line is skipped instead of counted with wrong values.

hints.title: Speed
hints.body: A while read loop that does the work in bash is much slower than awk on 100,000 lines, and starting cut or grep once per line is slower still. Let one awk program do the reading and counting, and sort do the ranking.

hints.title: The ShellCheck warnings in the starter
hints.body: Look up each code on the ShellCheck wiki. The fix is in the code, not in a disable comment.

hints.title: set -o pipefail and head
hints.body: sort | head -n 5 can kill sort with SIGPIPE when there is a lot of output. With pipefail and set -e that ends the script early. Test with a big log.

localTest.intro: From the challenge folder, with bash, Python 3, ShellCheck and bats-core 1.5 or later:
localTest.commands:
./summarize.sh sample/access.log
shellcheck summarize.sh
SANDBOX=none SOLUTION_DIR="$PWD" bats grade/summarize.bats
